nature_of_this_phase: S5 is explicitly NOT a new feature phase. epistemic_note_on_this_record: This certification record was written by the session that performed rounds 8-13 of the remediation loop directly and has full, freshly-verified working knowledge of them (every finding, every live reproduction, every commit). Rounds 5-7 and the initial 49 sme-s5 commits (the S5 phase's own opening implementation and first hardening sweep, predating the discrete 's5rN' round-labeling convention) are represented here by their own commit messages -- which are ground truth, independently re-derivable at any time via 'git log 50d6b0f..11137e6' -- and by characterizations carried forward from this session's own prior context, which was itself compacted at least once. Where this record states something about rounds 1-7 beyond what a commit message itself says, treat it as carried-forward summary, not a freshly re-verified claim, and prefer reading the actual commits/diffs over this record's own prose for anything load-bearing about that range.
review_loop_summary: The S5 phase ran a repeated discover-remediate-verify loop per its own section 13 mandate: a multi-dimension adversarial Opus 5 review (6 parallel dimension-reviewers plus an adversarial verify pass, in later rounds run via the Workflow tool) finds and confirms blocking findings against the current HEAD; the implementing session fixes ONLY the confirmed findings, runs the affected tests plus a full regression pass, commits; a fresh review (no memory of the prior round's own reasoning) runs again against the new HEAD. This repeated for 13 rounds. Raw/confirmed-blocking finding counts for the rounds this session directly ran (8 through 13): round 8 (7 raw / 5 confirmed), round 9 (4/4), round 10 (7/5), round 11 (8/4, two of which were a regression from round 10's own fix, S5R11-SF-B1), round 12 (7/5), round 13 (9/8 -- the highest since round 7, driven by the newly-discovered S5R13-SILENT-B1 numeric-correctness class plus continued spread of the 'unhedged status/action-mismatch guidance' pattern). The loop terminated at round 13 because round 13's own remediation commit (11137e6) then received a FRESH, independent, six-axis Opus 5 verification review (a different review shape than the standard 6-dimension hunt, since its job was specifically to verify the remediation rather than hunt for new defects) that returned zero CONFIRMED_FAIL axes and zero blocking incidental findings -- see review_rounds[12] below for its full detail.

review_rounds.note: Findings from this period are represented only by the 49 'fix(sme-s5)'-prefixed commits above (b23e500 through f752e85), several of which self-reference finding IDs like S5R3-VOCAB-B3, S5R4-SHARE-01 in their own subject lines, confirming a review-and-remediate loop was already running before the commit-message convention settled on the explicit 's5rN' prefix used from round 5 onward. Recurring themes visible directly in those 49 commit subjects: fetch-failure-vs-empty-state hardening (the single largest cluster -- 'X read paths throw instead of masking failure as empty', repeated across at least 6 separate commits), unbounded .in()/list truncation at Postgres/PostgREST's implicit row caps (repeated across at least 8 separate commits, the same defect class S5R7's own chunking commits continued), dataset-supersession detection and guidance, evidence-removal race conditions (at least 3 separate commits), and verification-prose-scan compliance. This record does not re-itemize each individual finding from this period beyond what the commit subjects themselves already state.

review_rounds.summary: S5R11-SF-B1: round 10's own fix (making revokeAppSession/persistAppSession throw on a genuine DB error) had an unintended consequence -- opaque-session-cookies.ts's setAll() is wired by @supabase/ssr's createServerClient as an internal onAuthStateChange callback invoked from inside GoTrueClient's own _notifyAllSubscribers, which re-throws anything that isn't an AuthError; proxy.ts (the Next.js middleware, matching nearly every route) calls supabase.auth.getUser() with no try/catch, so a throw from deep inside setAll() propagated as an uncaught exception crashing the middleware for that request on any transient DB blip. Live-verified via directly driving the real SDK call chain. Fixed by making setAll() itself never throw (graceful degradation), while revokeAppSession/persistAppSession themselves continue to throw for their other direct/awaited callers, which still need that. Also fixed FILED_RECORDED's null-report copy (previously grouped with READY, actually reachable via a distinct, genuinely different path) and hedged the shipment page's own LOCKED-line captions.

review_rounds.remediation_approach: One bounded remediation pass covering all 8 confirmed-blocking findings, per this codebase's own section 13 discipline: implement only the confirmed findings, run affected tests plus full regression, commit, then invoke one fresh independent review against the exact new HEAD before declaring done. S5R13-SILENT-B1 was fixed by converting resolveGoodSectorForActualLine's return type to a discriminated ResolveGoodSectorResult (OK-with-sector vs FETCH_FAILED), forcing every caller (calculateLine, reproduceCalculationResult's resolveCnCodeForLine sibling, get-default-reference-for-line.ts) to explicitly handle a genuine fetch error rather than silently folding it into 'sector unknown'; calculateLine now rejects with FETCH_FAILED before ever reaching the persistence call. The six guidance findings (A-1 x2, B-1, C-1, D-1, E-1) were fixed with ONE shared structural rule instead of six independent patches: src/domain/shipments/recovery-availability.ts's recalculateAvailability/redetermineAvailability functions, derived directly from record_calculation_result's own SQL (the READY carve-out fires purely on whether a calculation_results row already exists at the currently-running engine version -- independently live-verified, including the specific combined edge case of a calc predating an engine bump AND separately redetermined, which a naive two-axis 'why is it stale' model -- the shape round 13's own reviewers themselves proposed -- would have answered wrong). Two new CompletenessBlocker fields (shipment_status, calculation_engine_is_current) and a shared blockerRecoveryHint function let completeness-report-card.tsx and declaration-actions.tsx consult one source instead of diverging. S5R13-EVID-B1 was fixed by threading verificationStatus through EvidenceSection/EvidenceFileRow and replacing the Remove control with a static locked notice once VERIFIED, via a new evidenceRemovalLocked predicate mirroring the live RLS policy exactly -- the RLS policy and application-layer rejection themselves were left untouched.

summary: PASS_WITH_NOTES. S5 ran a 13-round adversarial discover-remediate-verify loop against the entire S1-S4 product surface, per its own explicit section 13 mandate never to self-certify and never to stop at a merely-plausible fix. This session directly ran and has full working knowledge of rounds 8 through 13 (rounds 1-7 are represented by their own commit history and carried-forward session summary -- see epistemic_note_on_this_record above). Round 13, the final round, found the highest confirmed-blocking count since round 7 (8, plus 1 yellow): a newly-discovered numeric-correctness defect (S5R13-SILENT-B1, a swallowed DB fetch error silently skipping the Annex II direct-only exclusion rule and persisting a 20%-over-inclusive regulatory figure), and six related instances of a recurring 'unhedged status/action-mismatch guidance' pattern that had already been individually patched a dozen-plus times across 12 prior rounds without ever being closed structurally. This round's remediation (commit 11137e6) fixed S5R13-SILENT-B1 by making the swallowed fetch error fail closed with a typed, compiler-enforced FETCH_FAILED outcome, and closed the six guidance findings with ONE shared, SQL-derived domain rule (src/domain/shipments/recovery-availability.ts) instead of six more independent patches -- a rule proven, via live reproduction against real Postgres, to be MORE precise than what round 13's own reviewers themselves proposed (a naive two-axis 'why is it stale' model that gets a real combined edge case wrong). An eighth finding (evidence-removal dialog honesty) was fixed by threading real verification status through to the UI without touching the underlying RLS/application-layer lock. Before committing, the full verification battery (typecheck, full unit/integration suite, production build, full E2E suite) ran clean except for one already-documented, environment-rooted flake unrelated to this phase. After committing, one FRESH, independent Opus 5 review -- six parallel adversarial verification axes plus a synthesis pass, targeting specifically the six things the governing spec named (persisted-number correctness, DB error fail-closed behavior, READY stale-repair semantics, UI-surface agreement, evidence-deletion honesty, P14 protection) -- independently re-derived and re-reproduced every one of the remediation's own load-bearing claims against real Postgres rather than trusting the commit message, and returned CONFIRMED_PASS on all six axes with zero blocking incidental findings. One confirmed-yellow finding (S5R13-SILENT-Y1) was deliberately not remediated this round, per the round's own explicit scope, and is recorded above as a disclosed, non-blocking, tracked follow-up. P14's protected regulatory zone was confirmed untouched at every one of the 13 rounds' own commits, independently re-confirmed by round 13's own fresh review against the final commit. The D2 authorization gate was respected throughout: never inferred, never built. This certification authorizes nothing beyond the review itself. Per S5's own governing specification -- explicit and more restrictive than S4's -- this phase ends here: no deploy, no merge, no production release, no push, no further S5 or post-S5 implementation work, at any point, regardless of this PASS_WITH_NOTES verdict.
